newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iranian exiles hold anti-Tehran session in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iranian exiles hold anti-Tehran session in Iraq.

text.p: Iranian exiles have ended a seven-day meeting in Baghdad discussing how to increase resistance to the government in Tehran, a statement by the Iraq-based Mujahideen organisation said on Thursday.
It said 487 members of what it termed Iran's parliament in exile met to discuss what the heavily armed exiles could do to overthrow the Iranian government.

"The session by the National Council of Resistance (NCR) came at a crucial time when important decisions had to be made with regard to activities inside Iran and preparations by the National Liberation Army (NLA) to overthrow the mullah's regime," Mohammad Mohadessin, chairman of the group's foreign affairs committee, told Reuters.

Mariam Rajavi, proclaimed by the exiles as future president of Iran, attended the session along with her husband, the NCR chairman. The statement said the members saw live-fire exercise by its NLA forces near Iran's border.
Baghdad provides refuge to the Mujahideen, who moved to Iraq in the 1980s during the eight-year Iraq-Iran war. They have mounted raids across the border into Iran, drawing Iranian reprisal attacks.
